title: Configuration
description:
You can pass a — what we call universal — configuration object to fine-tune your API reference.

It is universal because it works in all environments: pass it to the JS API directly, or use it in one of the integrations.

example.caption: Working with just an HTML file, that is how you pass the configuration:

sections.title: API Documents
sections.description: There is just one thing that is really required to render at least something: the content. There are a couple of ways to pass your API document.

sections.title: Properties
sections.description: Configuration properties to customize the behavior and appearance of your API reference.

sections.title: Methods
sections.description: Custom functions to control specific behaviors and URL generation.

sections.title: Events
sections.description: Callback functions that are triggered by user interactions and system events.

url.description:
Pass an absolute or relative URL to your API document. This can be JSON or YAML.

It is the recommended way to pass your API document: in most cases the document can be cached by the browser, so subsequent requests are fast even as the document grows.

content.description: Directly pass an API document (JSON or YAML) as a string.

x-doc.note: While this is convenient for a quick setup, it may hurt performance for large documents. Prefer `url` for those.

sources.description: Add multiple API documents to render all of them. We need a slug and title to tell them apart in the UI and in the URL — omit them and we will do our best anyway.

x-doc.footer: The first entry is the default one. When the list is generated, set `default: true` to pick another.

title.description: Shown in the UI. Falls back to `API #1`, `API #2`, …

slug.description: Used in the URL. Generated from the title or the index when omitted.

url.description: Absolute or relative URL to the API document.

default.description: Makes this the document rendered first.

authentication.description: To make authentication easier you can prefill the credentials for your users.

x-doc.footer: `preferredSecurityScheme` also accepts an array (OR) or an array of arrays (AND/OR) for more complex relationships.

preferredSecurityScheme.description: Which security scheme(s) should be used by default.

darkMode.description: Whether dark mode is on or off initially (light mode).

documentDownloadType.description: Sets the file type of the document to download. Set it to `none` to hide the download button.

x-doc.footer: When `direct` is passed, it just outputs a regular link to the passed URL.

hideModels.description: Whether to show the models section at the bottom of the page.

layout.description: The layout to use for the references.

searchHotKey.description: Key used with `CTRL`/`CMD` to open the search modal.

proxyUrl.description: Making requests to other domains is restricted in the browser and requires CORS headers. A proxy is used to work around that.

spec.description: The old way to pass an API document.

x-doc.note: Use `url` or `content` instead. `spec` still works and is migrated automatically, with a console warning.

telemetryKey.description: Internal build-time key. Never written by users.

generateHeadingSlug.description: Customize how heading URLs are generated. The function receives the heading and returns the string id that controls the entire URL hash.

x-doc.note: This must be passed through JavaScript — setting a data attribute will not work.

examples.caption: Default behavior, resulting in the hash `#description/heading-slug`:

customFetch.description: Custom fetch function used both when loading the API document and when sending "Test Request" calls from the API client. Use it to add headers, attach credentials, or handle auth.

x-doc.type: (input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

onLoaded.description: Fired when the references are fully loaded.

onBeforeRequest.description: Fired before the outbound request is sent from the embedded API client. Mutate `requestBuilder` to change method, path, query, headers, and body.

x-doc.note: **Experimental:** `RequestFactory` may change in minor releases. Treat its fields as unstable until the API stabilizes.
